rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose noun for people coming together again, especially family or close groups.

example.english: The whole family can finally have a reunion over dinner on New Year's Eve.
example.traditional: 一家人喺年三十晚返齊食飯，終於可以團聚。
example.jyutping: jat1 gaa1 jan4 hai2 nin4 saam1 sap6 maan5 faan1 cai4 sik6 faan6 zung1 jyu1 ho2 ji5 tyun4 zeoi6

rows.note: Use this more formal noun for reuniting after a period of separation, including a reunion event.

example.english: After years apart, family and friends finally had a reunion.
example.traditional: 多年離散後，親友終於重聚。
example.jyutping: do1 nin4 lei4 saan3 hau6 can1 jau5 zung1 jyu1 cung4 zeoi6

rows.note: Use this when the reunion is presented mainly as a planned social gathering rather than emphasizing the separation beforehand.

example.english: This Saturday we're holding a reunion and inviting all our former colleagues back.
example.traditional: 今個星期六我哋搞個聚會，叫晒以前啲同事返嚟。
example.jyutping: gam1 go3 sing1 kei4 luk6 ngo5 dei6 gaau2 go3 zeoi6 wui6 giu3 saai3 ji5 cin4 di1 tung4 si6 faan1 lai4

rows.note: Use this specifically for a class or school reunion.

example.english: Ten years after graduating, we finally held a reunion.
example.traditional: 畢業十年，我哋終於搞咗次同學會。
example.jyutping: bat1 jip6 sap6 nin4 ngo5 dei6 zung1 jyu1 gaau2 zo2 ci3 tung4 hok6 wui2
